text: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE July 13, 2026 Idaho Lawmakers Begin Work on Idaho's Nuclear Energy Future BOISE, Idaho — Members of the Idaho Legislature met today to begin defining the Legislature's role in shaping Idaho's future as a national leader in advanced nuclear research, technology, and energy. The meeting brought together Representative Ted Hill, Representative Josh Tanner, Senator Dave Lent, Senator Kevin Cook, and Senator Van Burtenshaw. Representatives from the Idaho Attorney General's Office, the Office of Lieutenant Governor Scott Bedke, and Idaho National Laboratory (INL) also participated in the discussion. The primary purpose of the meeting was to clarify the role the legislative branch will play in developing public policy and supporting the continued advancement of nuclear research and energy in Idaho. The group discussed a legislative report presented to the Governor's Advanced Nuclear Task Force. The report identifies national trends, Idaho's unique strengths, and potential policy options that would enhance Idaho's leadership in the nuclear industry. The report highlighted Idaho's unique position as home to Idaho National Laboratory, the nation's premier nuclear research laboratory, and outlines the growing demand for reliable, affordable electricity to support Idaho's growing population, manufacturing, agriculture, data centers, and national security. It also identifies workforce development, permitting coordination, research partnerships, infrastructure planning, and public engagement as key areas where state policy can help prepare Idaho for the future. "This meeting marks the beginning of an important conversation," said Senator Kevin Cook. "Idaho has an incredible opportunity to help lead America's Nuclear Renaissance, but we want to do it the right way. Our responsibility is to develop thoughtful public policy that protects Idaho citizens, supports innovation, creates high-paying jobs, and ensures Idaho remains a leader in nuclear research and energy." Senator Dave Lent added, "The goal is to ensure Idaho is prepared to meet growing energy needs while maintaining the state's longstanding commitment to public safety, environmental stewardship, and responsible innovation." Lawmakers emphasized that while the federal government maintains authority over nuclear licensing and safety, Idaho has an important role to play in workforce development, economic development, state permitting coordination, infrastructure planning, and building strong partnerships with industry, local governments, higher education, and federal agencies. The discussion builds upon SCR 120, which was approved by the Idaho Senate on a voice vote and by the Idaho House on a 59-9-2 vote during the 2026 legislative session, affirming legislative support for continued advanced nuclear research, demonstration, and responsible development in Idaho. The working group will continue meeting over the coming months to evaluate policy options, gather input from stakeholders, and identify legislative priorities for future legislative sessions. As interest in advanced nuclear technologies continues to grow across the United States, Idaho is uniquely positioned to remain at the forefront of research, innovation, workforce development, and America's energy future. Senator Dave Lent (Member of Governor's Idaho Advanced Nuclear Task Force, Senate Education Chairman) Representative Ted Hill (Member of Governor's Idaho Advanced Nuclear Task Force) Senator Van Burtenshaw (Senate Resources Chairman) Senator Kevin Cook
